record.title: Odd-characteristic quadratic-function design conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime with $p\equiv3\pmod4$, let $m\geq3$ be odd, and set $q=p^m$. Let $\ell$ be a positive integer satisfying $\frac{m-2}{4}\leq\ell\leq m-1$ and $\gcd(\ell,m)=1$. Define $f(x)=x^{p^{\ell}+1}$ and let $\mathbb{D}(f(x),k)=({\operatorname{GF}}(q),\mathcal{B}_{(f(x),k)})$. **Odd-characteristic quadratic-function design conjecture.** The incidence structure $\mathbb{D}(f(x),k)$ is a $2$-$(q,k,\frac{k(k-1)}{2})$ design, where

$$
k=q-\frac{pq-1}{2(p+1)}.
$$

This is the complementary conjecture for the odd-characteristic case; the supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Can Xiang, Xin Ling and Qi Wang, “Combinatorial t-designs from quadratic functions”, arXiv:1907.06235 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06235

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Fibonacci prefix antipower conjecture
record.statement: Let $F_n$ be an even Fibonacci number, where the Fibonacci numbers satisfy the usual recurrence, and let $\mathbf{f}$ denote the Fibonacci word. A **$k$-antipower** is a concatenation of $k$ pairwise distinct blocks of equal length. **Fibonacci prefix antipower conjecture.** There is an $(F_n-1)$-antipower with block length $\frac{F_n}{2}+F_{n-1}$ that is a prefix of $\mathbf{f}$. Based on the supplied text, this is an empirical conjecture about explicit antipower prefixes of the Fibonacci word; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Swapnil Garg, “Antipowers in Uniform Morphic Words and the Fibonacci Word”, arXiv:1907.10816 (2021).

record.title: The NP-completeness conjecture for the Sigma-1 theory of Young's lattice
record.statement: Let $\textbf{Y}=\left\langle \mathcal P,\leq\right\rangle$ be Young's lattice, where $\mathcal P$ is the set of partitions ordered by inclusion of their Young diagrams. The **Sigma-1 theory conjecture.** The $\Sigma_1$-theory of Young's lattice $\textbf{Y}=\left\langle \mathcal P,\leq\right\rangle$ is $\textbf{NP}$-complete. The preceding discussion establishes that this theory is at least $\textbf{NP}$-hard if it is decidable; the conjecture asks for the matching upper bound. An affirmative answer would give an $\textbf{NP}$-characterization of the posets that embed in Young's lattice.
record.source_name: Alexander Wires, “Complexity in Young's Lattice”, arXiv:1907.13360 (2019).

record.title: Inverse extremal conjecture for restricted signed sumsets containing zero
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of $k$ non-negative integers, where $k\geq 5$ and $0\in A$, and let $h$ be a positive integer satisfying $3\leq h\leq k-1$. The **restricted signed sumset** $h\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$ consists of sums formed by assigning distinct elements of $A$ the signs $+$ or $-$.

**Inverse conjecture.** If

$$
|h\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A|=2hk-h(h+1)+1,
$$

then

$$
A=d*[0,k-1]
$$

for some positive integer $d$.

This conjecture characterizes equality in the proposed lower bound when the set contains zero. The paper proves analogous equality classifications for special cases, but the full inverse statement remains open.
record.source_name: Jagannath Bhanja, Takao Komatsu and Ram Krishna Pandey, “Direct and inverse results on restricted signed sumsets in integers”, arXiv:1908.00081 (2019).

record.title: Janzer's conjecture on blowups of spiders
record.statement:
Let $s\geq2$, $k,b,t\geq1$ be integers. Let $S$ be an $s$-legged spider whose longest leg has length $k$, and suppose that $e(S)=(s-1)k+b$, where $0\leq b\leq k$. Let $t*S$ denote the union of $t$ copies of $S$ sharing the designated roots as in the spider blowup construction. **Janzer's conjecture.** 
$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,t*S)=O\left(n^{1+\frac{s-1}{(s-1)k+b}}\right).
$$
 This conjecture concerns extremal numbers of blowups of spiders and is motivated by results for subdivisions of complete bipartite graphs and related graphs. The source presents it as an open conjecture.

record.title: Postnikov's 5-adic valuation conjecture for Morse link numbers
record.statement:
Let $L_n$ denote the Morse link numbers, and let $\xi_5$ denote the 5-adic valuation. Let $\alpha=\dotsc 111111120_5$ be a 5-adic integer.

**Postnikov's 5-adic valuation conjecture.** For $n\geq 4$,

$$
\xi_5(L_n)=
\begin{cases}
2 & \text{if } n \text{ is even},\\
\xi_5(n-\alpha)+3 & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

This is attributed to Postnikov; the source notes that the original formulation contains typographical errors, but supplies no resolution of the corrected statement.

record.title: Complex Lu–Wenzel even partial-sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M(n,\mathbb{C})$ be the space of complex $n\times n$ matrices, with Frobenius norm $\|X\|=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(XX^*)}$. For $X\in M(n,\mathbb{C})$ with $\|X\|=1$, let $T_X(Y)=[X^*,[X,Y]]$ and order its eigenvalues as $\lambda_1(T_X)\geq\lambda_2(T_X)\geq\cdots$. **Complex Lu–Wenzel even partial-sum conjecture.** For

$$
k=1,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{2}\right\rfloor,
$$

one has

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{2k}\lambda_i(T_X)\leq 2k+2.
$$

The source presents the complex formulation as an analogue of the real Lu–Wenzel conjecture and proves the equivalence relations among the complex versions; it does not state a proof of the complex conjecture itself.
record.source_name: Jianquan Ge, Fagui Li, Zhiqin Lu and Yi Zhou, “On some conjectures by Lu and Wenzel”, arXiv:1908.06624 (2019).

record.title: One-corner conjecture for rearrangements of 1-Naples parking functions
record.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let a parking preference be represented by its associated lattice-path diagram, with corners defined as turns of the path. Suppose that there is only one corner above the line $y=n-x$. **One-corner conjecture.** That parking preference and all of its rearrangements are elements of $PF_{n,1}$. This conjecture concerns the characterization and enumeration of rearrangements of decreasing $k$-Naples parking functions that remain $k$-Naples parking functions. The paper presents it as an open conjecture for the case $k=1$.

record.title: The reticulation lower-bound conjecture for tree-metrizable minimal support networks
record.statement: Let $N(B)$ be a tree-metrizable minimal support network of a biconnected component $B$, and suppose that $N(B)$ has $n$ leaves. A **reticulation arc** is an arc entering a reticulation vertex. **Reticulation lower-bound conjecture.** The network $N(B)$ has at least $n-2$ reticulation arcs. This conjecture would provide a quantitative constraint on tree-metrizable minimal support networks and could give deeper insight into the mathematical structures behind tree-metrizability. The source presents it as an unresolved conjecture and gives no known proof or disproof.

record.title: Ionin–Shrikhande conjecture for Ryser design parameters
record.statement:
A **Ryser design** on $v$ points is a collection of $v$ proper subsets, called blocks, of a $v$-point set such that every two blocks intersect in the same number $\lambda$ of points, with $\lambda<v$, and at least two block sizes occur. The parameters $v$ and $\lambda$ denote the number of points and the common block-intersection size, respectively.

**Ionin–Shrikhande conjecture.** For any Ryser design on $v$ points,

$$
4\lambda-1\leq v\leq\lambda^2+\lambda+1.
$$

This conjecture is presented as a conjecture of Ionin and Shrikhande in the paper. The supplied text gives no resolution, so its status is open.
record.source_name: Tushar D. Parulekar and Sharad S. Sane, “Some results on the Ryser design conjecture-II”, arXiv:1909.03504 (2019).

record.title: The cycle rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $C_t$ be the cycle on $t$ vertices, and let $f_{C_t}(s,s)$ denote the least number of independent sets of size $s$ in $C_t$ that guarantees a rainbow independent set of size $s$. **Cycle rainbow matching conjecture.** If

$$
s<\frac{t}{2},
$$

then

$$
f_{C_t}(s,s)=s.
$$

The source presents this as a possible explanation for the jump between the almost-full and full rainbow matching problems.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Joseph Briggs, Jinha Kim and Minki Kim, “Rainbow independent sets in certain classes of graphs”, arXiv:1909.13143 (2019).

record.title: The exceptional-line-graph rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f_G(n,m)$ denote the least number of independent $n$-sets in a graph $G$ that guarantees a rainbow independent set of size $m$. **Exceptional-line-graph conjecture.** If $G$ is the line graph of a graph and is not a graph as in Example, then

$$
f_G(n,n-1)=n-1.
$$

The source explains that the excluded construction is an obstruction to the stronger bipartite statement and that this conjecture would imply the general-graph full-matching conjecture.

record.title: The quarter-order bound for power domination in connected hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}=(V(\mathcal{H}),E(\mathcal{H}))$ be a connected hypergraph on at least four vertices, with every edge $e\in E(\mathcal{H})$ satisfying $|e|\geq 3$. Write $\gamma_{P}(\mathcal{H})$ for its power domination number and $\gamma_{P_{I}}(\mathcal{H})$ for its infectious power domination number.

**Quarter-order bound.**

$$
\gamma_{P_{I}}(\mathcal{H})\leq\gamma_{P}(\mathcal{H})\leq\frac{|V(\mathcal{H})|}{4}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the observation or infection step improves the general domination bound from $|V(\mathcal{H})|/3$ to $|V(\mathcal{H})|/4$ for connected hypergraphs whose edges all have size at least three. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.

record.title: Enumeration conjecture for geometric multi-chains of t-filters
record.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $T_n=\{(i,j)\mid 1\leq i<j\leq n\}$ be the triangular poset with $(i,j)\preceq(k,l)$ if and only if $i\geq k$ and $j\leq l$. For $t\in[n]$, let $T_{n,t}=\{(i,j)\in T_n\mid j>t\}$, and let $(V_m,V_{m-1},\ldots,V_1)$ be a geometric multi-chain of $t$-filters, meaning a nested tuple of filters satisfying the two geometricity conditions defined for the triangular poset.

**Enumeration conjecture.** The number of geometric multi-chains of $t$-filters $(V_m,V_{m-1},\ldots,V_1)$ is

$$
\frac{mt+1}{mn+1}\binom{(m+1)n-t}{n-t}.
$$

This conjectural formula gives a closed enumeration of the geometric multi-chains used in the proposed combinatorial description of the $H$-triangle. The supplied text does not state whether the formula has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Identifiability conjecture for Fin and Wing submodels of cycle graphs
record.statement:
For $n\geq 3$, let $G$ be a graph obtained from the $n$-compartment cycle graph by adding one or more incoming edges or one or more outgoing edges. Let $In=Out=\{1\}$ and $Leak=\emptyset$.

**Fin-and-Wing submodel conjecture.** The linear compartmental model $(G,In,Out,Leak)$ is generically locally identifiable.

The coefficient maps for these submodels are complicated, so the paper does not analyze their Jacobians completely. It proves identifiability for certain families of added edges and conjectures the broader statement for models with more than one or two incoming or outgoing edges.
record.source_name: Seth Gerberding, Nida Obatake and Anne Shiu, “Identifiability of Linear Compartmental Models: The Effect of Moving Inputs, Outputs, and Leaks”, arXiv:1910.13549 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.13549

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2019). “Second, the effect of removing a leak remains an open question: the authors conjectured that removing a leak from certain models preserves identifiability .”

record.title: Ramsey robustness conjecture for Ramsey-infinite graphs
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, let $H$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ denote the family of $r$-Ramsey-minimal graphs for $H$. Let $\beta_r(H;G)$ be the Ramsey robustness of $G$ with respect to $H$. A graph $H$ is **$r$-Ramsey-infinite** when $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is infinite. **Ramsey robustness conjecture.** If $H$ is $r$-Ramsey-infinite, then

$$
\inf\{\beta_r(H;G):G\in\mathcal{M}_r(H)\}=0.
$$

Equivalently, the only possible reason for robustness to be bounded away from zero over $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is that $H$ is $r$-Ramsey-finite. The conjecture is motivated by constructions with arbitrarily small robustness, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Victor Souza, “Blowup Ramsey numbers”, arXiv:1910.13912 (2021).

record.title: Graver's maximality conjecture in dimension three
record.statement: Let ${\cal R}_{3,n}$ be the generic $3$-dimensional rigidity matroid on $E(K_n)$, and let an abstract $3$-rigidity matroid be an abstract $d$-rigidity matroid with $d=3$. **Graver's maximality conjecture.** The generic $3$-dimensional rigidity matroid is the unique maximal abstract $3$-rigidity matroid on $E(K_n)$. The conjecture is a long-standing open problem for $d=3$; the corresponding general conjecture is false for $d\geq4$.

record.title: A large independent set of low-degree vertices in non-chorded connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a **non-chorded connected graph** of order $n$, and let an **independent set** be a set of vertices no two of which are adjacent. 

**Low-degree independent set conjecture.** $H$ contains an independent set $I$ of order at least $n/6$ such that every vertex of $I$ has degree at most $2$ in $H$.

The conjecture would strengthen the paper's preceding lemma, which guarantees a smaller independent set of low-degree vertices in every non-chorded connected graph. Its status is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Point-line incidence conjecture for even-cycle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be an integer. Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a set of $n$ lines in the plane. Define the incidence set and incidence graph by

$$
I=I(P,\mathcal{L})=\{(p,\ell)\in P\times\mathcal{L}:p\in\ell\},\qquad G=(P\cup\mathcal{L},I).
$$

The **incidence graph** has vertex parts $P$ and $\mathcal{L}$, and is $C_{2k}$-free when it contains no cycle of length $2k$.

**Point-line incidence conjecture.** If $G$ is $C_{2k}$-free, then

$$
|I(P,\mathcal{L})|=o\left(n^{1+1/k}\right).
$$

This conjecture asks whether the geometric setting admits a bound strictly smaller than the general extremal-graph upper bound. The paper presents it as an open problem and develops lower-bound constructions for point-line arrangements with prescribed girth.
record.source_name: Mozhgan Mirzaei, Andrew Suk and Jacques Verstraëte, “Constructions of point-line arrangements in the plane with large girth”, arXiv:1911.11713 (2019).
record.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019). “For $k \in \{2,3,5\}$, it is known that $\ex\left(n, C_{2k}\right)=\Theta\left(n^{1+{1}/{k}}\right)$(see for $k=2$ and for $k\in \{3,5\}$). It is a long standing open problem to determine the orde”

record.title: Generalized face-uniformity bound for two-valued functions on Hamming graphs
record.statement:
Let $f: \{0,\ldots,q-1\}^n \rightarrow \{0,1\}$ be a function with $B$ zeros and $C$ ones, where $q\geq 3$. Suppose that for some $k$, every $k$-face has the same number

$$
\frac{Cq^k}{B+C}
$$

of ones of $f$. **Generalized face-uniformity bound.** If

$$
\frac{B+C}{\gcd(B,C)}>q,
$$

then

$$
k\geq\frac{n}{q+1}+1.
$$

This is proposed as a more general form of the perfect-coloring bound, applying to any two-valued function; the case $q=2$ is identified with the known correlation-immunity bound, while the cases $q>2$ remain open.
